Query CockroachDB as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__cockroachdb.R
oauth_db_cockroachdb.Rd

Read CockroachDB data using each visitor's JWT access token and database permissions. Works with self-hosted and cloud clusters configured for cluster SSO using JWTs. Returns an RPostgres connection for DBI or dbplyr.

Usage

oauth_db_cockroachdb(
  authorization,
  host,
  dbname,
  user,
  ...,
  port = 26257L,
  sslrootcert = NULL,
  connect_timeout = 5L,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

host

One CockroachDB SQL hostname or IP address.

dbname

Database name, not a connection string or URI.

user

SQL username, or a function deriving it from the selected sign-in. The cluster must map the token's principal to that user.

...

RPostgres result options (bigint, check_interrupts, timezone, timezone_out), application_name, or TCP keepalive options. Authentication, connection identity and TLS settings cannot be overridden.

port

SQL port, default 26257.

sslrootcert

CA certificate bundle path, or NULL for libpq's configured bundle.

connect_timeout

Connection timeout in whole seconds, at least two.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function, usually named con. Call connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression, then pass the connection to DBI. Before sign-in, the function waits quietly.

Details

Install RPostgres linked to libpq 16 or later. Configure the cluster's server.jwt_authentication settings for your provider's issuer, signing keys, audience and principal claim. Request a JWT-format access token intended for the cluster. Opaque access tokens and ID tokens aren't used by this helper. There is no universal CockroachDB OAuth client preset.

Connections use verified TLS and CockroachDB's JWT-as-password protocol, with --crdb:jwt_auth_enabled=true. The helper requires password authentication from the server and doesn't use client certificate or trust authentication. Unset PGSERVICE and PGSERVICEFILE before use. This helper doesn't use the newer SASL OAUTHBEARER protocol.

Create the helper inside server() and call con() before each query. After token renewal, the next call replaces the connection with current credentials without replaying completed reactive queries. Account or username changes, lost permissions, sign-out and session end close it. Complete a transaction on the connection that started it; get the next operation's connection through con().

See also

vignette("cockroachdb", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_cockroachdb(
  auth$connection,
  host = "cluster.example.org", dbname = "reporting",
  user = function() {
    reference <- shiny::req(auth$connection())
    identity <- reference$identity(claims = "preferred_username")
    shiny::req(identity$id_token_claims$preferred_username)
  },
  sslrootcert = "path/to/ca.pem"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user")
})
} # }
